knowledge_abstraction.bug_theme: Per-dimension spatial parameter mapping inconsistency under non-default padding modes
knowledge_abstraction.general_principle: Operators that accept per-dimension spatial parameters may incorrectly map values to spatial axes when a non-default execution mode changes the underlying code path, causing a parameter to be applied along the wrong dimension.

risk_dimensions.shape: Unequal height and width padding values; non-square spatial input shapes; degenerate or small spatial dimensions that can reveal dimension-specific padding effects.
risk_dimensions.dtype: Floating-point and integer dtypes may expose shape or index calculation differences, but the primary risk is dimension mapping independent of dtype.
risk_dimensions.memory: Non-contiguous or strided inputs may interact with padding logic; however, the core risk is parameter-to-axis mapping rather than memory layout.
risk_dimensions.device: CPU and CUDA backends may have separate padding implementations with different dimension mapping behavior.
risk_dimensions.execution_state: Forward execution with non-default padding modes such as circular or reflect can activate alternate padding code paths.

failure_mechanism.description: A padding tuple interpreted in an inconsistent spatial axis order causes padding to be applied along the wrong spatial dimension for certain padding modes, leading to incorrect output shape or values.

input_exploration: Explore asymmetric multi-dimensional padding configurations where per-dimension values differ
Vary input spatial shapes so height and width effects can be distinguished
Swap height and width padding amounts to detect dimension-order confusion
Use multiple non-default padding modes with asymmetric padding parameters
constraint_awareness: Padding parameters are often required to be tuples with length matching the number of spatial dimensions
Non-default padding modes may use different code paths than zero padding
Output shape and padded regions should follow the documented dimension order
oracle_strategy: Compare against a reference implementation that applies padding explicitly along the intended spatial dimension
Check output spatial shape and padded boundary values for incorrect dimension ordering
Monitor for inconsistent behavior between equivalent dimension configurations after swapping height and width

transferability.reason: Many operators accept per-dimension spatial parameters such as padding, kernel size, stride, and dilation; dimension-order or axis-mapping inconsistencies can occur across APIs and backends, especially when alternate execution modes are involved.

important_considerations: Probe dimension-order handling for multi-dimensional padding parameters, not just whether padding produces a shape change
Use non-default padding modes because they may invoke separate code paths with different axis mapping
Separate height and width observations by using distinct spatial sizes and asymmetric padding amounts
Consider backend-specific differences in spatial parameter mapping
generation_strategy: Generate parameter combinations that vary per-dimension padding values and padding modes, and use reference-based oracles to verify that each dimension is padded according to the documented axis order.
